2. By the impugned award, against a claim of Rs. 20,74,588/-, the learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.
04,05,618/- as compensation for the damages in favour of the appellant/claimant.
3. As per pleadings of the claim application filed under Section 166 of the MV Act, the appellant is the owner of Guru Nank Dharamkata, which is situated at Village Kodiya.

On the date of accident on 21.01.2015, the offending truck bearing registration No. MH-31-CB-4496 loaded with paddy, came to the Dharamkata of the appellant for measuring of weight, at that time, the said offending vehicle was driven rashly and negligently by the respondent No. 1, on which the said truck turned turtle and Jaydeep Singh Kanda vs Kamlesh Sahu on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112916488/
1 fall over the building attached to the Dharamkata Machine, resulting to damages in the Dharamkata Machine and also damage caused to the building.

sentences.text: The matter was reported to the Police and crime No. 14/15 was registered and charge-sheet was filed and charges were accepted by the respondent No. 3.
On the date of accident, the vehicle was insured with the respondent No. 3 and ownership of respondent No. 2.
Thus, an amount of Rs. 20,74,588 was sought as compensation for the damages.
4. The claim application was resisted by the respondents on various grounds.
5. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned Tribunal framed issue and decided the same in favour of the appellant/claimant and awarded the above stated compensation by the impugned award.
6. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that on the date of accident the entire building attached to the Dharamkata Machine has been destructed and Dharmkata machine has also been damaged.

Learned Tribunal failed to award any amount towards the bill Ex.P-24 which is with regard to repair of Dharamkata Machine, however, appellant has incurred Rs.1,97,000/- toward repairing of the Dharamkata machine.

7. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that learned Tribunal has erred in awarding lum-sum compensation of Rs. 1 lakh for the damages to the building, which is highly inappropriate and the same is meager.
Further learned claim tribunal has awarded less compensation towards loss caused to the appellant due to closure of the Dharamkata till the period of revival.

The amount of Rs.
30,000/- is meager amount for the loss caused to the appellant.

8. Learned counsel for respondent No.3 opposing the submission of counsel for the appellant and would submit that Dharamkata machine was purchased by the appellant in the year 2014 as per receipt Ex.P- 18 and 19 of Rs.1,61,015/-, whereas appellant has claimed Rs.1,97,000/- for repairing of the said Dharamkata machine, which is more than the purchase amount of the said machine .
He further submits that the learned Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation.

9. Heard learned counsel for the parties, considered their rival submissions and perused the record with utmost circumspection.
10.Learned Tribunal has awarded the compensation as under:
 Sl. Heads Calculation  No.
 1. For loss of income during Rs. 30,000/-
 closure of dharamkata
2 . For Destruction of building Rs. 1,00,000/-/-

11.The tribunal while passing the impugned order recorded a finding that 'Ex.P-24 is the bill of Rs.1,97,000/- for repair of Dharamkata Machine dated 03.03.2015 which is more than the total amount of purchase bills of Dharamkata Machine i.e. Ex.P-18 and Ex.P-19 which is Rs. 1,61,051/-
and thus the same cannot be accepted'.
12.Perusal of receipt Ex.P-18 and 19 shows that Dharamkata machine was purchased by the appellant in the year 2014 of Rs. 1,61,015/-
13.Perusal of the bill (Ex.P-24)
would show that appellant has incurred Rs. 1,97,000/- for repairing of Dharamkata machine, which was damaged in the alleged accident.

14.This Court is of the opinion that the machine was totally damaged, for which he would have definitely spent the amount for repairing of the same, and the Tribunal ought to have considered the bill (Ex.P-24).

Hence the appellant is entitled to get the amount i.e. Rs. 1,00,000/- which he incurred towards repairing of the Dharmakata Machine towards Bill (Ex.P-24).
15.True, it is that the earnings of the appellant definitely would have been affected because the building got destructed as well as loss caused to the appellant due to closure of the Dharamkata.
16.The
Tribunal has granted Rs. 1,00,000/- towards destruction of building, this Court is assessing additional amount of Rs. 75,000/- for the same (total amount of Rs. 1,75,000/-).
This Court is also assessing Rs. 45,000/- instead of 30,000/- towards loss caused to the appellant during closure of the Dharmakata for a period of three months.

17.In view of the aforesaid observations, this Court is computing the compensation as below :-
 S.N. Particular Awarded by this Court

For Bill Ex.P-24 1,00,000/-
4. For loss of Income during the 15,000x3 = 45,000/-
 period of closure of Dharamkata  for three months

Total Compensation Rs. 5,95,618/-

3 18.For the forgoing reasons, the appeal is allowed in part.

4,05,618/- awarded by the tribunal is enhanced to Rs. 5,95,618/-.

Hence, after deducting the amount of Rs. 4,05,618/-, the Appellant is held entitled to get for an additional amount of Rs.
1,90,000/-, the additional amount shall carry interest @6% per annum from the date of claim application.
The insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced amount of compensation within 60 days.
Rest of the conditions of the impugned award shall remain intact.
19.In the result, the appeal is allowed in part.
